summary: Program missions can await a replicated daemon startup capability with Fractal.awaitDaemon({ host, feature, minVersion, version? }): the newest owner-origin daemon.started claim resolves the durable wait without polling.

replay.detail: The await-daemon host request adopts a durable registration and journals its exact startup claim result under the caller key. Completed keys replay without rereading capabilities; resumed open attempts retain their tuple.

schema.detail: No client schema, generated code, table or migration changes. Internal program.step claims hold registrations and results.

rules.detail: The wait observes an owner-origin startup fact; it grants no authority and performs no upgrade, service restart or health probe.

compatibility.detail: New bundles using awaitDaemon need execution daemons and bundled hosts supporting await-daemon. Existing run, ask and awaitPr contracts retain their meaning.

downtime.detail: No runtime deployment is performed. Normal host replacement adopts open registrations.

manual.detail: Update execution daemons before publishing bundles using this primitive. minVersion orders numeric feature versions; optional version matches the exact advertised build string, not Git ancestry.

recovery.detail: Cancellation removes the attempt's in-memory interest without an external watch. daemon.started is not proof of current liveness, readiness or completion of a particular activation; those need separate run-bound facts.
